subject: Operating Systems
title: CPU Scheduling — quick revision
content:
CPU SCHEDULING — QUICK REVISION

Goal: choose a ready process for CPU execution. Common criteria include CPU utilization, throughput, turnaround time, waiting time and response time.

FCFS: non-preemptive; simple; may suffer from the convoy effect.

SJF: selects the process with the shortest next CPU burst. It minimizes average waiting time under ideal assumptions, but long jobs may starve.

Round Robin: preemptive; each process receives a time quantum. A very large quantum approaches FCFS; a very small quantum increases context-switch overhead.

Priority scheduling: highest-priority process runs first; aging can reduce starvation.

Exam checklist: distinguish waiting time from turnaround time; draw the Gantt chart; calculate completion, turnaround, waiting and response times carefully.

subject: DBMS
title: Relational keys — quick revision
content:
RELATIONAL KEYS — QUICK REVISION

Superkey: any set of attributes that uniquely identifies a tuple.

Candidate key: a minimal superkey; removing any attribute means it no longer uniquely identifies tuples.

Primary key: the candidate key selected as the main identifier.

Alternate keys: candidate keys not chosen as the primary key.

Foreign key: attribute(s) whose values refer to a candidate/primary key in another or the same relation, subject to the schema's constraints.

Exam checklist: uniqueness alone is not enough for a candidate key; minimality is also required.

subject: Probability and Statistics
title: Basic probability — quick revision
content:
BASIC PROBABILITY — QUICK REVISION

For a finite sample space with equally likely outcomes, P(A) = number of outcomes in A divided by total outcomes.

Complement: P(Aᶜ) = 1 − P(A).

Addition rule: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).

If A and B are mutually exclusive, P(A ∩ B) = 0. If independent, P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B). These are different conditions.

Conditional probability: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B), when P(B) > 0.

Exam checklist: do not confuse mutually exclusive events with independent events.
